text:
The color of a common crow is black.

The wind howled around Lara, stripping away the last remnants of her fatigue. She stood at the precipice, the world below a tapestry of greens and grays, but her eyes were drawn to a single, sharp silhouette against the pale sky. A crow, perched on a jagged outcrop, stared back with eyes like polished obsidian. Its feathers were not merely black; they were a void, a deep, iridescent ink that seemed to absorb the light and the noise of the climb. In that moment, the bird’s stark, monochromatic presence mirrored the clarity Lara felt within herself—a pure, unadulterated focus that cut through the chaos of the ascent. The crow let out a harsh, guttural call, a sound that was both warning and welcome, anchoring her in the present, in the beauty of the simple, undeniable truth of its dark plumage.
